name: drift-audit-cycle-for-materialized-implications
claim: Materialized implications require periodic drift audits to confirm their effects still hold; the audit is a first-class maintenance cycle, not a one-off.
invariants: A drift audit iterates over implications with non-null materialized field, re-evaluates whether the action's effects are still present, and either bumps materialized.last_verified to the audit date or emits a new primitive asserting the drift and proposing a re-materialization action
Audit cadence is case-dependent - some implications (module splits) decay slowly, others (bash removal) decay faster; default cadence TBD, initial proposal quarterly with per-implication overrides

evidence.detail: Materialization as a historical-only fact implies that some mechanism must periodically re-verify effects or the graph accumulates false claims of current success. The drift audit is that mechanism, paired with the materialization principle as its execution layer.

Atomization migration (plans/atomize): claim restated to the norm; enumerable content moved to invariants. Previous claim: Materialized implications require periodic drift audits to confirm their effects still hold. A drift audit iterates over implications with non-null `materialized` field, re-evaluates whether the action's effects are still present (code still shaped as intended, bash still absent, modules still split, etc.), and either bumps `materialized.last_verified` to the audit date or emits a new primitive asserting the drift + proposes a re-materialization action. The audit is a first-class maintenance cycle, not a one-off. Audit cadence is case-dependent: some implications (module splits) decay slowly; others (bash removal) decay faster if the team isn't vigilant. Default cadence TBD; initial proposal is quarterly with per-implication overrides.
